sa.question: Square of side 14 cm has four semicircles on sides as diameters. Find area of shaded region inside square.
In figure, ABCD is a square of side 14 cm. Semi-circles are drawn with each side of square as diameter. Find the area of the shaded region.
sa.model_answer: Area of the square ABCD = 14 x 14 = 196 cm² Area of semicircle AOB=1/2 x πr² =1/2×22/7x7x7 Similarly, area of semicircle DOC = 77 cm² Hence, the area of shaded region (Part W and Part Y) = Area of square -Area of two semicircles AOB and COD = 196 – 154 = 42 cm² Therefore, area of four shaded parts (i.e. X, Y, W, Z) = (2 x 42) cm² = 84 cm²

sa.model_answer: Area of ΔOAB=√3/4(side)²=√3/4 x (12)² =36√3=36 x 1.73 =62.28 cm² area of circle with center O =πr²=3.14 x (6)² =3.14 x 36 =113.04 cm² area of sector(OLQP)=πr² x θ/360°=3.14 x 6² x 60°/360° =3.14 x 36 x 1/6 =18.84 cm² area of shaded region=area of ΔOAB+area of circle-2 area of sector OLQP =(62.28+113.04-2 x 18.84)cm² =137.64cm²

la.question: ABCD is a rectangle of length 10√2 cm and breadth 5√2 cm. A semicircle is drawn on AB as diameter, and APB is the isosceles triangle inscribed in that semicircle. The shaded region is the part of the semicircle outside the triangle. Find its area.
la.model_answer: The radius of the semicircle is 5√2 cm, so its area is 25π cm². The triangle has base 10√2 cm and height 5√2 cm, so its area is 50 cm². The shaded area is 25π − 50 cm².
